quote: Theorem 2. Let T and T* denote the lifetimes of two networks with signature vectors s = (s1, . . . , sn) and s* = (s*1, . . . , s*n), respectively. Suppose that the components of networks fail based on GCPs with MVFs Λ(t) and Λ*(t), respectively. If s ≤st s* and Λ(t) ≥ Λ*(t) for all t ≥ 0, then T ≤st T*.
model: other: coherent network lifetimes under geometric counting process (GCP) failures
family: GCP arrival-time mixtures weighted by signature
compared: network lifetimes via signature st-ordering + MVF ordering

quote: Theorem 3. For two networks as described in Theorem 2, assume that the failure of components of both networks appear according to the same GCPs: 1. If s ≤st s*, then T ≤st T*, 2. If s ≤hr s*, then T ≤hr T*, 3. If s ≤rh s*, then T ≤rh T*, 4. If s ≤lr s*, then T ≤lr T*.

hypotheses.text: same GCP for both networks; s ≤st s*

quote: 2. If s ≤hr s*, then T ≤hr T*.
compared: network lifetimes via signature hr ordering

quote: 3. If s ≤rh s*, then T ≤rh T*.
compared: network lifetimes via signature rh ordering

quote: 4. If s ≤lr s*, then T ≤lr T*.
compared: network lifetimes via signature lr ordering

quote: From part (ii) of Theorem 3, since hr-ordering implies mrl-ordering, we conclude that if s ≤hr s* then T ≤mrl T*.
compared: signature hr ordering ⟹ network mrl ordering

quote: Example 3. Consider two networks with signature vectors s = (0, 2/3, 1/3) and s* = (1/3, 0, 2/3). It is easy to see that s ≤mrl s*. However, s ⋡st s* and hence s ⋡hr s*. Assume that the components of both networks fail based on the same GCPs with MVF Λ(t) = t². Then, a straightforward calculation gives E(T) = 2.5525 > E(T*) = 2.4871, which, in turn, implies that T ⋡mrl T*.
family: 3-component networks; GCP with MVF Λ(t) = t²
compared: s ≤mrl s* but s not st/hr-ordered; conclusion fails

conclusion.direction: T ⋡_mrl T* (E(T) = 2.5525 > E(T*) = 2.4871) — s ≤hr s* cannot be weakened to s ≤mrl s*

quote: Theorem 5. Consider a network whose components fail based on two different GCPs with MVFs Λ(t) and Λ*(t), respectively. Denote by s(t) and s*(t) the corresponding conditional signatures of the two networks. Then, • s(t) and s*(t) are increasing in the sense of st-ordering with respect to t; • Λ(t) ≤ Λ*(t) implies that s(t) ≤st s*(t) for all t ≥ 0.
model: other: conditional signature s(t) = (P(T = ϑk | T > t))

hypotheses.text: GCP failures; s(t) the conditional signature

conclusion.direction: s(t) increases in st order as t grows

ambiguity: s(t) treated as a discrete distribution over {1,...,n}.

quote: • Λ(t) ≤ Λ*(t) implies that s(t) ≤st s*(t) for all t ≥ 0.
compared: conditional signatures under different GCP intensities

quote: Theorem 7. Let s(t) and s*(t) be the conditional signatures of two networks with lifetimes T and T*, respectively. Suppose that the component failure in both networks appear based on the same GCPs. 1. If s(t) ≤st s*(t), then (T − t| T > t) ≤st (T* − t| T* > t); 2. If s(t) ≤hr s*(t), then (T − t| T > t) ≤hr (T* − t| T* > t); 3. If s(t) ≤rh s*(t), then (T − t| T > t) ≤rh (T* − t| T* > t); 4. If s(t) ≤lr s*(t), then (T − t| T > t) ≤lr (T* − t| T* > t).
model: other: residual lifetimes of used networks

conclusion.direction: (T − t | T > t) <=_st (T* − t | T* > t)

quote: Lemma 2. Assume that {ξ1(t), t ≥ 0} and {ξ2(t), t ≥ 0} are two GCPs with intensity functions λ1(t) = λ1 > 0, and λ2(t) = λ2 > 0, respectively. Let ϑ1,1, ϑ1,2, . . . and ϑ2,1, ϑ2,2, . . . denote the arrival times corresponding to the two processes, respectively. If λ1 ≥ λ2, then (ϑ1,1, . . . , ϑ1,n) ≤st (ϑ2,1, . . . , ϑ2,n) for every n ≥ 1.
family: geometric counting processes, constant intensities λ1 ≥ λ2
compared: joint st ordering of arrival-time vectors
ambiguity: Proof uses MTP2 density ratio and Theorem 6.B.8 of Shaked–Shanthikumar.

quote: Theorem 8. Consider two three-state networks that each consist of n components having signature matrices S1 and S2, respectively. Let the components of ith network fail according to GCP {ξi(t), t ≥ 0}, i = 1, 2 with intensity function Λi(t) = λi. Let ϑi,1, ϑi,2, ... denote the arrival times corresponding to {ξi(t), t ≥ 0}. Suppose that (T1^(1), T2^(1)) and (T1^(2), T2^(2)) are the corresponding state lifetimes of the two networks, respectively: • If λ1 ≥ λ2 and S1 ≤uo S2, then (T1^(1), T2^(1)) ≤uo (T1^(2), T2^(2)), • If λ1 ≥ λ2 and S1 ≤st S2, then (T1^(1), T2^(1)) ≤st (T1^(2), T2^(2)).
model: other: three-state network lifetimes (T1 time in up-state, T2 lifetime)
compared: joint state lifetimes under signature-matrix uo ordering
joint state lifetimes under signature-matrix st ordering

quote: Theorem 9. Let T1 be the lifetime of a three-state network in state K = 2 and T2 be the lifetime of the network. Let the components failure of the network appear according to the GCP {ξ(t), t ≥ 0} with arrival times ϑ1, . . . , ϑn. • If I and J are PQD, then T1 and T2 are PQD. • If I and J are associated, then T1 and T2 are associated.
compared: dependence between the two state lifetimes

hypotheses.text: I, J PQD (the numbers of failed components at state transitions)

ambiguity: Dependence transfer rather than a distribution ordering; included as a stated ordering/dependence claim.
